title: Fact-Check: Is the NBA Investigating Domantas Sabonis Over Recent Performances?
text:
Fact-Check: Is the NBA Investigating Domantas Sabonis Over Recent Performances? - BasketballNews NBA Play Hoops Rank NBA Play Hoops Rank Home / NBA Fact-Check: Is the NBA Investigating Domantas Sabonis Over Recent Performances?
 By
 Ubong Richard Nov 18, 2026, 3:03 PM CUT
 Imago
 IMAGO / ZUMA Press Wire
 Verdict : No credible report supports it. Before the NBA's investigation into Kings coach Doug Christie's intentional foul on Seth Curry ended, the league's own statement found that Christie "made no intentional effort to give the Warriors a shooting foul." That probe showed the league will look into on-court behavior that appears suspicious, but it cleared the Kings. The claim that Domantas Sabonis is under investigation after a scoreless night against the Magic is far less substantiated.
 The rumor is built on a real game. Sabonis played 24 minutes against the Magic on Tuesday, attempted two field goals and missed both, one of them a 3-pointer. He also missed two free throws. He still grabbed two rebounds and dished out five assists. 
 The claim then goes a step further, saying league sources told reporters the NBA is probing whether he went scoreless on purpose because of sports betting. As of Wednesday, no outlet in the coverage reviewed carries that report, and the NBA has issued no statement about Sabonis.
 What the coverage does say points elsewhere. Analyst Kevin O'Connor wrote on X that Sabonis "doesn't want to be there," and the "quiet quitting" label spread quickly. That is a claim about effort and a possible trade request, not about gambling. 
 Nothing in that reporting connects Sabonis to a bettor, a sportsbook or a suspicious wager. The jump from "quiet quitting" to a betting probe appears to come from social media speculation rather than from any league source.
 The rumor does have a precedent that explains why it spread. The league investigated Raptors forward Jontay Porter in 2024 for betting irregularities, including the possibility that he bet the under on his own performances. One of the games involved was a scoreless outing in which multiple betting accounts tried to wager $10,000 to $20,000 on Porter unders. 
 Porter was later banned for life. A zero in the box score looks similar on its face, but in Porter's case the red flag was abnormal betting activity, and no one has reported anything comparable for Sabonis.
 The context around Sabonis also supplies other explanations. The Kings are 1-12 this season, and Sabonis has been in trade talk since last season. He told NBC Sports Bay Area that he was "shocked" to see his name in offseason reports. His contract adds to the strain, as he is owed $45.4 million this season and $48.6 million next, which makes a deal hard to find. 
 The Athletic's Sam Amick has reported that the Kings are willing to listen to offers for nearly anyone except rookie Darius Acuff Jr. A player in that position, on a team losing that often, can easily have a bad night.
 Domantas Sabonis Has More Mundane Explanations for His Scoreless Night
 The simplest explanation is physical. Sabonis is still recovering from the injury and surgery that kept him out for most of last season, and he reportedly missed the game before the Magic matchup because of ankle issues tied to that injury. 
 He says he is 100%, but a player returning from a recent absence, with minutes that change nightly, will often take fewer shots and score less.
 Role is another factor. Sacramento is moving away from using him as the focus of its offense, and the team's scoring is flowing through Darius Acuff Jr. and Zach LaVine. A center whose touches are reduced doesn't get many chances to score. Two shot attempts in 24 minutes look alarming in a box score, but it is consistent with a player who was passing more (five assists) rather than looking for his own shot.
 The context also matters before accepting any betting angle. A real investigation involves some mix of unusual betting patterns, sportsbook alerts and a formal league statement, and none of those has been reported for Sabonis. 
 The Porter case began only after those signals appeared, and ESPN and the league confirmed it publicly. The Christie case, which was about a different kind of suspicious behavior, was publicly acknowledged and resolved. If an NBA probe into Sabonis existed, it would be expected to follow a similar pattern.
 For now, the verdict on the claim that the NBA is investigating Sabonis is that it is unproven. The evidence available favors injury recovery, a reduced role, and trade-season frustration. The "quiet quitting" debate may continue as long as his minutes and the Kings' losing continue.
 A betting probe, though, would have to be confirmed by the league or an established reporter, and neither has done that.
